version.changelog:
- Refactored all documentation and instructions from English to Chinese for improved localization.
- Updated descriptions, workflows, report generation steps, and best practice guidelines with Chinese text and terminology.
- No changes to scripts or core review workflow logic; functionality and structure remain the same.
- Maintains full feature parity, including automated/deterministic analysis, report generation, and cross-platform support.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a coherent code-review helper, but its optional HTML report can execute injected browser code from untrusted findings.

dimensions.detail: The scripts recursively read source files under the selected target path and optionally write a report file. No network access, credential-store access, or unrelated environment probing was found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, dependency installation, remote retrieval, or package execution setup was found; metadata.json is empty.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow asks the agent to read target code and run local Python scripts, which is expected for code review. The trigger language is broad and whole-directory scans should remain user-directed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background worker, scheduled task, shell persistence, privilege escalation, memory modification, or tool hijacking behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated code-review purpose matches the bundled scanners and reference documents, but the HTML report generator embeds untrusted project, category, file, type, and JSON finding data into HTML/script contexts without sufficient escaping.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the skill read the code paths you explicitly ask it to review. Treat generated HTML reports as potentially unsafe when reviewing untrusted repositories or finding JSON; open them cautiously or fix the escaping issue first.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: generate_report.py directly inserts untrusted report data into HTML and script contexts, creating a credible stored-XSS risk when opening generated reports.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the package includes complexity analysis, pattern scanning, references, and report generation aligned with code review. Some capability claims are broad, but I found no hidden or unrelated behavior.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: the referenced markdown files are present locally and were inspected completely.
[AR3] expected: Overridden: the cited text is security-review example content such as debug mode and vulnerable-code examples, not instructions to bypass evaluator or agent safety rules.
[TM1] expected: Overridden: shell=True and similar strings appear as vulnerable patterns to detect in reviewed code, not as commands the skill executes.
[EA1] expected: Overridden: references to arbitrary code execution describe vulnerability severity criteria, not a grant of unrestricted tool authority.
[LP3] expected: Partly applicable as guidance: the skill does not declare a formal tool allowlist, but its requested local file reads and Python script runs are disclosed and proportionate to code review.
[SQP-1] expected: Minor scope note: trigger phrases are broad, but the body consistently frames use around reviewing code, diffs, PRs, or repositories.
[SQP-2] expected: Minor disclosure note: recursive source reading and deliberately insecure examples are expected for this skill, but users would benefit from clearer warnings.
[SQP-3] expected: Not material: the instructions are primarily Chinese, while the report generator supports Chinese, English, or bilingual output.
